states.name: North Carolina
states.headline: First statewide subsidy rate floor in the nation takes effect October 1, 2026 — but the gain is rural, and a directed study of decoupling star ratings from reimbursement is the largest quality-related revenue risk in the portfolio.
states.agency: DHHS / Division of Child Development and Early Education
states.ratevintage: 2023 market rate study — floor arriving Oct 2026
states.qris: Star Rated License → 'Pathways to the Stars' (Jul 2025). Rates published by county AND star level. Decoupling plan directed, due May 1 2026.
states.prek: NC Pre-K, mixed delivery. ~$7,117 state spending per child. $0 new funding in FY2026-27 plus an unfunded dyslexia screening mandate.
states.politics: All 170 legislative seats on the ballot. House Republicans are one seat from a veto-proof majority. Gov. Stein not up until 2028.
watch: Model the county-by-county rate floor impact before October 1 — metro sites may capture nothing
Get DCDEE on record on post-rescission payment basis
Obtain the May 1, 2026 QRIS decoupling report
Inventory Pathways consultation dates; test whether Pathway 3 lets national accreditation reduce assessment burden
November 3 — House seat 72 decides whether deregulation proceeds over a veto

states.name: Georgia
states.headline: Georgia Pre-K — lottery-funded, roughly half privately delivered, ten of ten national quality benchmarks — is the strongest public revenue line in the footprint. CAPS has simultaneously contracted to the lowest initial eligibility threshold in the country.
states.agency: Bright from the Start: DECAL — licensing AND CCDF lead agency
states.ratio4: 1:18 (max group 36) — among the most permissive nationally
states.elig: 30% of SMI — lowest initial threshold in the US
states.ratevintage: 60th percentile; 2024 analysis of 2023 data. New cost survey in field now.
states.waitlist: No published waitlist — access rationed by eligibility threshold
states.qris: Quality Rated (1–3 stars). Mandatory for CAPS funding since Dec 31, 2021. Framework revision status unconfirmed.
states.prek: Georgia Pre-K: $594M in FY2027, ~50% private delivery, 70,572 children, $30,000 startup grant per new classroom, 10/10 NIEER benchmarks.
states.wage: $7.25 federal floor; median $13.35/hr. Pre-K salary parity with K-12 pulls the whole building's wage floor up.
states.session: January 2027 — new two-year term; all prior bills die
states.politics: Kemp term-limited. Rick Jackson (R) def. Lt. Gov. Burt Jones in the June 16 runoff; Keisha Lance Bottoms (D). Jones was the architect of Georgia's entire child care tax agenda.
watch: Get into the DECAL / Georgia Policy Labs cost survey sample — it resets the CAPS rate benchmark
Resolve enrollment vs. attendance with DECAL; model an attendance/arrears reversion across 76 centers
Watch retention of Commissioner Jacobs and the identity of the new Lt. Governor (controls Senate referral)
Engage Sen. Chuck Payne on the SB 554 capital-grants refile; consider attaching a zoning provision
Model HB 1123 wraparound exposure at private Georgia Pre-K sites

states.name: Arizona
states.headline: Subsidy waitlist up 575% in 24 months and still growing faster than appropriations can clear it. First Things First's tobacco-tax revenue base is structurally decaying. A constitutionally indexed minimum wage compounds both.
states.agency: ADHS Bureau of Child Care Licensing / DES Child Care Assistance
states.agencyhead: ADHS Dir. Debbie Johnston (3rd in 3 yrs); DES Dir. Michael Wisehart
states.elig: 165% FPL — well below the federal ceiling
states.ratevintage: 2022 survey (75th pct infants / 50th pct all other ages). A 2024 survey exists and is unused.
states.qris: Quality First. 3+ stars unlocks a 40% subsidy rate enhancement — worth $25.66/day per subsidised infant. Appropriation-dependent, not an entitlement.
states.prek: No state pre-K program. ESA vouchers exclude typically-developing 3s and 4s; the disability pathway and ESA-funded transitional-K are the openings.
states.wage: $15.15 (Jan 2026), CPI-indexed annually with no legislative off-ramp
states.politics: Hobbs (D) vs. Biggs (R), rated Tossup to Lean D. All 90 legislative seats. Two competing ESA measures on the November ballot.
watch: ADHS 24-hour annual training compliance deadline is THIS MONTH — audit all 30 sites
November 3 — Governor plus HCR 2048 plus the Protect Education Act
DES response to the federal rescission; the 40% quality enhancement is the easiest line to trim
Press for a rate rebase to the unused 2024 survey in the FY2028 request cycle
The 2027 minimum wage is announced ~Sept/Oct — model it now

states.name: Texas
states.headline: The only state in the portfolio that already built and paid for the payment architecture the 2024 federal rule required — $50M spent on the transition. The open question is whether TWC keeps it now the mandate has lapsed.
states.agency: HHSC Child Care Regulation / TWC via 28 local workforce boards
states.ratevintage: 2025 survey — CURRENT. Higher of 75th pct or Cost of Quality baseline.
states.qris: Texas Rising Star, mandatory since Oct 2022. +5/+7/+9%. Entry gate is licensing compliance; also gates the property tax exemption.
states.prek: Half-day pre-K via the Foundation School Program. HB 2 mandates 85% passthrough to private providers and anti-crowd-out verification, but removed full-day ADA protection.
states.session: January 2027 — 140 days, writes the FY2028–29 budget
states.politics: Abbott. Senate committee turnover: Education K-16 Chair Donna Campbell; Economic Development Chair Angela Paxton. Interim charges give child care unusual prominence.
watch: The 40 TAC Chapter 809 final rule — does TWC keep enrollment-based prospective payment?
Governor's Task Force report due December 1, 2026 — it frames the whole 2027 debate
Whether Texas voluntarily keeps the 7% copay cap
SEMARC background-check operationalisation — confirm the screening vendor is ready
Property tax exemption per site: requires TRS participation AND ≥20% subsidy census

states.name: Florida
states.headline: VPK is a privately delivered public programme — 77% of providers are private. That is the political asset. It sits alongside the sharpest cost-versus-revenue divergence in the report: the wage floor rises 25% while the VPK allocation holds at $3,029.
states.agency: DCF licenses (63 of 67 counties); DOE Division of Early Learning runs subsidy and VPK
states.agencyhead: DEL Chancellor Cari Miller; Commissioner status unresolved
states.ratio4: 1:20 — NO statutory group-size caps; square footage governs
states.copay: Exceeds 7%; providers may bill families above copay
states.ratevintage: Annual legislative adoption; rates 11–15% BELOW the 75th-percentile benchmark
states.qris: CLASS-based programme assessment. 4.00 composite is a contract gate, not a star rating — and 99% pass, so it is a floor not a screen. Differential capped at 15%.
states.prek: VPK: $433.8M, 153,132 children. Base student allocation $3,029 — FLAT for three consecutive years. 41st of 43 states on per-student spending.
states.wage: $14.00 now; $15.00 on September 30, 2026 — final Amendment 2 step, then CPI-indexed
states.politics: DeSantis term-limited; Donalds (R) leads, rated Solid R. 2027 is a new Governor's first session.
watch: Confirm Florida let enrollment-based and prospective payment lapse — waivers expired August 1
September 30 — minimum wage hits $15.00 against a flat $3,029 VPK allocation
Autumn 2026 interim committee weeks — obtain the calendar the day it posts
Revive HB 345 / SB 512 VPK inflation indexing — a bipartisan sponsor pair is rare in Tallahassee
Obtain the child care tax credit cap and confirm the SB 738 municipal special assessment exemption is applied

states.name: Arkansas
states.headline: The most urgent item in the report: the sustainability funding package expires September 30, 2026 with no successor in the public record, no session until January 2027, and a fiscal session that declined to add early childhood money.
states.agency: Dept of EDUCATION — DESE Office of Early Childhood (moved from DHS under LEARNS)
states.agencyhead: Interim OEC Director Ashelyn Abney; Dep. Comm. Stacy Smith
states.elig: Sliding by SMI; 30 hrs/week work requirement
states.copay: Zero at/below poverty; 7% multi-child cap status unconfirmed
states.ratevintage: Restructured Oct–Nov 2025; 75th percentile, higher in Benton/Washington
states.qris: Better Beginnings, now 1–6. Level 2 is the price of admission — losing it terminates subsidy immediately. Tiers 3–4 and 5–6 collapsed: only 2→3 and 4→5 move the rate.
states.prek: Arkansas Better Chance: $5,105/child/yr center-based, 40% match, 15% admin cap. Thin to loss-leading absent in-kind match. Mostly public-school delivered.
states.wage: $7.25 federal floor; state wage data unconfirmed
states.politics: Sanders (R) seeking a second term, rated Solid R. Planning assumption: continuity. LEARNS framework persists.
watch: THE SEPTEMBER 30 CLIFF — model a 10–20% subsidy rate reduction now
Resolve whether the 7% copay cap was adopted
Obtain the rate table, Better Beginnings 4–6 criteria, and the Early Childhood Commission roster
Position for the 2027 United WE / OEP licensing-streamlining bill via Sen. Breanne Davis
Track the ABC rate-floor rematch and its funding source; confirm the $14.0M expiring federal recovery money has a replacement

states.name: Oklahoma
states.headline: Eligibility cut from 85% to 55% of SMI on July 1; 131 centers closed since April. But HB 4298 (approved May 12, 2026) gave operators gap-fee authority and ratio relief, and — uniquely — district pre-K enrollment is FALLING, with children staying in child care centers.
states.agency: Oklahoma Human Services, Child Care Services
states.ratio4: 1:10 reported — Appendix GG could not be retrieved, UNCONFIRMED
states.copay: $0–$473/mo; provider must collect before the state pays
states.ratevintage: Effective January 1, 2023 — unrevised for 3.5 years against +27% infant cost inflation
states.waitlist: Unconfirmed — rationed via application freeze and eligibility cut
states.qris: Reaching for the Stars, five levels. The STEEPEST rate tie in the portfolio: infant 1★ $20.00 → 5★ $50.60/day. The 2★→3★ step alone is +67%.
states.prek: Near-universal school-based 4-year-old pre-K — but enrollment fell from 39,767 (2019-20) to 32,794 (2024-25). NIEER cites children remaining in child care centers.
states.wage: $7.25; educators earn $11–12/hr. HB 2778 gives them free child care.
states.politics: Stitt term-limited and was the veto point. Republican runoff August 25: Drummond vs. Mazzei. Munson (D). Either successor is likely less hostile.
watch: HB 4298 gap-fee federal approval and OKDHS billing guidance — confirm the operative effective date and do not bill early
OKDHS rulemaking on master teacher ratios — file comments; the flexibility level is being set now
The August 25 Republican runoff — cheapest campaign access available
Fallout from the 55% SMI cut: attrition, receivables, and distressed 3★+ acquisition targets
HB 1979 task force appointments — seek an industry seat before they close

states.name: Virginia
states.headline: The most improved environment in the portfolio: waitlist eliminated, statutory biennial re-benchmarking enacted, and the best-priced public revenue stream anywhere — Mixed Delivery at $19,441 a slot, reserved for licensed private providers.
states.agency: VDOE Office of Child Care Health and Safety; VDSS operations
states.agencyhead: Supt. Jenna Conway — an early childhood person running K-12
states.ratio4: 1:10 — among the tightest in the portfolio
states.copay: 5% cap — BELOW the former federal ceiling; $5/mo at or below poverty
states.ratevintage: Cost estimation model, rates unchanged since October 2022
states.waitlist: 12,144 (Dec 2025) → just over 2,000 (June 2026). Eliminated in the FY27–28 budget.
states.qris: VQB5 — mandatory for ANY site receiving public funds. 700 of 800 points are CLASS interaction scores. No rate differential. Ratings published publicly.
states.prek: VPI at $6,763/slot AND the Mixed Delivery Grant Program at $19,441/slot — contract-based, cost-of-quality, reserved for licensed non-faith-based private settings, ~2x oversubscribed.
states.wage: $12.77 now; $13.75 Jan 2027; $15.00 Jan 2028 — +17.5% over 24 months against frozen rates
states.session: January 2027 — short 'caboose' session amending the adopted biennium
states.politics: Democratic trifecta. NO House elections in Nov 2026 — Virginia holds them in odd years; next is November 2027.
watch: Confirm the 8VAC20-781 effective date, grace period and whether existing variances EXPIRE — this week
Get inside the SB 134 / HB 1208 re-benchmarking methodology before the numbers publish
Pursue Mixed Delivery expansion; obtain FY27 guidelines from VECF
Resolve enrollment vs attendance; obtain the two overdue workgroup reports
Shape the October 1, 2026 Commission report — it already endorses zoning and licensing simplification

states.name: Alabama
states.headline: One genuinely unusual feature: Alabama's Childcare Facility Tax Credit is written explicitly for FOR-PROFIT providers, is refundable, and scales with quality rating. It sunsets December 31, 2027.
states.agency: DHR Child Care Services (licensing/subsidy); ADECE (pre-K + Quality STARS)
states.agencyhead: DHR Comm. Nancy Buckner; ADECE Sec. Ami Brooks
states.elig: 60% SMI / 180% FPL — well below the federal ceiling
states.ratevintage: 70th percentile of the 2017 survey; schedule dated April 1, 2022 — NINE years stale
states.qris: Quality STARS, five levels. +2 to +10% subsidy. Also gates BOTH state tax credits, and the facility credit scales with star level.
states.prek: First Class Pre-K: $84,804–$97,908 per classroom annually plus up to $125,000 setup. 20 straight years at 10/10 NIEER benchmarks. 4,100 children waitlisted; 229 classrooms needed.
states.session: MARCH 2, 2027 — not January; first year of a four-year term
states.politics: Ivey term-limited. Tuberville (R) vs. Jones (D), rated Safe R. Entire Legislature on the ballot. Both agency heads serve at gubernatorial pleasure.
watch: The tax credit sunsets December 31, 2027 — the March 2027 session is the last practical vehicle
January 5, 2027 reservation window: first-come, first-served, largest pools ever ($20M / $5M), last under current law
Obtain the First Class Pre-K classroom count BY AUSPICE from ADECE (334-224-3171)
HB 78 screen-time rulemaking will land on licensed centers
November 3 cabinet consequences — 20 years of pre-K continuity rests on gubernatorial patronage

states.name: Tennessee
states.headline: Simultaneously the most legislatively productive and the most fiscally contractionary state. Two near-unanimous 2026 acts on red tape and dedicated revenue — while the quality bonus was cut so far that a top-scoring provider gained 0.8%.
states.agency: Tennessee Dept of Human Services, Child Care Services
states.copay: Universal 5% on EVERY approved family since Oct 1, 2025
states.ratevintage: New table effective January 1, 2026 — but 60th percentile basis
states.qris: Report Card (mandatory, four visits/yr, scores POSTED for parents) + voluntary Star-Quality. Bonus cut Jan 2026 from 15/20% to 5/10%.
states.prek: Voluntary Pre-K, ~935 classrooms, ~$85M. District-controlled: a 142-district business development effort. Three-star QRIS is the hard prerequisite.
states.wage: $7.25; average worker earnings $12,973/yr, 1 in 10 below poverty
states.politics: Lee term-limited — the single biggest variable. New governor writes the FY2027-28 budget. A new TDHS commissioner is likely.
watch: Obtain Public Chapter 997 (Promising Futures Act) before its January 1, 2027 provisions take effect
Obtain Public Chapter 980 and audit the development pipeline against its zoning amendments
Re-underwrite three-star status: the subsidy return fell from 20% to 10%; VPK access is the remaining case
Confirm payment basis with TDHS Child Care Fiscal (1-800-362-8004) and request the waitlist count
Two items already in effect and unexploited: PC 80 for-profit grant eligibility, and PC 873 youth employment

states.name: Kentucky
states.headline: The most consequential legislative cycle in the state's history. HB 6 became law without the Governor's signature — permanent free child care for child care workers, ECCAP privatisation, microcenters, a mandated cost model, and All STARS frozen under legislative control. The money did not grow.
states.agency: CHFS / DCBS / Division of Child Care
states.agencyhead: CHFS Sec. Dr. Steven Stack; DCC director unconfirmed
states.copay: Flat daily chart, $0 to a $25 maximum
states.ratevintage: 80th percentile, increased July 2021. Cost model mandated for FFY2028–2030.
states.qris: All STARS, five levels. Mandatory for any provider receiving public funds. $25–$45/mo per subsidy child at Levels 3–5. HB 6 froze agency discretion over the system.
states.prek: Kentucky Preschool Program: ~$170M over the biennium, frozen at 2019 levels. 704 KAR 3:410 expressly authorises district contracts with private preschools — under-exploited.
states.wage: $7.25 — no state minimum above the federal floor
states.politics: Beshear term-limited in 2027. Republican supermajorities override routinely. Every 2027 fight is positioning for the 2028 budget.
watch: ECCAP third-party administrator procurement — due December 1, 2026
Confirm the ~$40M/yr CCAP rate-maintenance appropriation survived HB 500; obtain the DCC-300
All STARS modernisation plan due October 1, 2026 — get on the stakeholder list first
Microcenter regulations July 1, 2027: only TEN statewide, restricted to experienced operators — literal first-mover advantage
Submit operator-side evidence to the HJR 50 Auditor regulatory review
